Title: GET /api/home backend endpoint — aggregated Home page payload

Repo: zealchaiwut/commander

## What & Why

The new Home page replaces today's Overview and needs aggregated data across all projects in a single payload: summary stats, project list with status, and a recent-activity feed. This ticket builds the backend endpoint that powers the Home page; frontend slices land in separate tickets and stub against this endpoint.

Shipping this ticket first unblocks all other Home page tickets.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] New endpoint `GET /api/home` returns a single JSON payload with three top-level keys: `stats`, `projects`, `activity`
- [ ] `stats` shape:
  - `sprint_running: {count: int, projects: [{name, sprint_label, elapsed_sec}]}`
  - `awaiting_uat: {count: int, projects: int, oldest_age_sec: int|null}`
  - `sprints_planned: {count: int, total_tickets: int}`
  - `backlog: {count: int, per_project: [{name, count}]}` — top 5 projects sorted desc by count
- [ ] `projects` shape: array of `{name, slug, icon, status: "running"|"uat-pending"|"idle", sprint_running?, last_sprint?, uat_count, backlog_count, last_activity_at}` — one entry per registered project
- [ ] `activity` shape: array of `{type, project, title, sub, timestamp, link}` limited to 5 most recent events across all projects
- [ ] Payload is computed server-side from existing GitHub data and local state files — no new DB tables
- [ ] Per-project sub-queries cached at 30s TTL with key `home:<project_slug>` to avoid hammering GitHub API on page refresh
- [ ] Cache is in-memory; rebuilds from scratch on dashboard restart
- [ ] Activity event types include at minimum: `sprint_started`, `sprint_completed`, `ticket_moved_to_uat`, `ticket_needs_rework`, `sprint_failed`
- [ ] `last_activity_at` for each project derives from "most recent of last sprint finish OR last ticket update" — no new field stored
- [ ] All timestamps in payload are ISO 8601 UTC strings
- [ ] Error handling: if a project's GitHub data fails to fetch, that project's entry has `status: "idle"` with counts of 0 rather than the whole endpoint returning 500

## UAT Test Steps

1. Hit `GET /api/home` with no projects registered.
   **Expected:** Returns `{stats: {sprint_running: {count: 0, ...}, ...}, projects: [], activity: []}`.

2. Hit `GET /api/home` with 2 projects, 1 running sprint, 3 UAT-pending tickets.
   **Expected:** `stats.sprint_running.count === 1`, `stats.awaiting_uat.count === 3`, both projects appear in `projects` array.

3. Hit the endpoint twice within 30 seconds.
   **Expected:** Second call is significantly faster (cache hit).

4. Wait 31 seconds, hit again.
   **Expected:** Fresh fetch from GitHub (cache expired).

5. Simulate one project's GitHub API failing.
   **Expected:** Endpoint still returns 200; the failing project has `status: "idle"` with zero counts; other projects render normally.

6. Verify `activity` array never exceeds 5 entries.

7. Verify all timestamps parse cleanly as ISO 8601 UTC.

## Out of Scope

- Frontend rendering (separate tickets)
- WebSocket / SSE for real-time updates — page refresh is enough for v1
- Pagination of activity feed beyond 5 events
- Per-user customization of cached data
- Audit logging of who hit the endpoint

## Notes for Implementer

- Reuse existing GitHub fetch helpers in `services/sprint_manager/` — don't create a new GitHub client
- The 30s cache should be a simple dict-with-timestamp pattern; no need for Redis
- If a project has no sprint history at all, `last_activity_at` should be `null` and the project's `status` is `"idle"`
- Test with at least 2 projects to verify per-project caching works independently
- This endpoint will be hit on every Home page load — keep it fast, budget <500ms cold, <50ms warm

Labels: enhancement, backend, dashboard, home, sprint-12

Title: Home page shell + 4 summary stat cards

Repo: zealchaiwut/commander

## What & Why

Build the Home page's top section: minimal header, three-section layout (Right now / Projects / Activity), and the 4 clickable summary stat cards. Projects deck and activity feed are separate tickets — this ticket stubs those sections as empty placeholders.

Mockup reference: `home_page_final.html` — section 1 (4 stat cards).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Page renders at temporary route `/home-preview` (final route swap happens in routing ticket)
- [ ] HTML page title: "Commander — Home"
- [ ] Page layout: three vertical sections with headers "Right now", "Projects · click to open", "Activity"
- [ ] Header is minimal: brand mark with `Commander` wordmark + green live-dot + 2 icon buttons (Bulk create, Settings). No subtitle. No tab strip.
- [ ] Body uses `padding: 32px 32px` on desktop, `20px` on mobile
- [ ] **4 stat cards in a responsive grid:**
  - Desktop (>1024px): 4 columns
  - Tablet (~700-1024px): 2 columns
  - Mobile (<700px): 1 column
- [ ] Each card has: small label with icon (uppercase, letter-spacing), big number (36px, mono font), contextual sub-line with bolded mono-font values
- [ ] **Card 1 — Sprint running** — icon `ti-player-play`. Big number is `stats.sprint_running.count`. When count >= 1: card has green border + animated flowing top stripe (copy from running sprint card CSS), background fades green→transparent. Sub-line: when count == 1, "<project-name> <sprint-label> · <elapsed> elapsed"; when count > 1, "<N> projects"; when 0, "None right now".
- [ ] **Card 2 — Awaiting UAT** — icon `ti-eye-check`. Big number is `stats.awaiting_uat.count`. When count >= 1: number rendered in amber color. Sub-line: "Across <N> projects · oldest <T> ago" (humanized relative time).
- [ ] **Card 3 — Sprints planned** — icon `ti-list-check`. Big number is `stats.sprints_planned.count`. Sub-line: "Ready to run · <N> tickets total".
- [ ] **Card 4 — Backlog** — icon `ti-inbox`. Big number is `stats.backlog.count`. Sub-line: per-project breakdown "<proj-1> <N> · <proj-2> <M>" (top 2; if >2, append "· +<K> more").
- [ ] Cards on hover: lift 1px (`transform: translateY(-1px)`), border darkens, box-shadow appears (`0 4px 12px rgba(0,0,0,0.04)`), cursor pointer
- [ ] Cards have minimum tap target of 44×44px on mobile
- [ ] Stat cards have `role="button"` and respond to keyboard Enter / Space
- [ ] **Click behavior** for v1:
  - Sprint running → navigates to `/project/<slug>/sprint-mgmt` for the first running project; no-op if 0
  - Awaiting UAT → navigates to the project with most UAT-pending tickets; no-op if 0
  - Sprints planned → tooltip only: "Open a project to plan sprints"
  - Backlog → tooltip only: "Open a project to view its backlog"
- [ ] Page fetches `GET /api/home` on initial load
- [ ] While loading: render skeleton placeholders (subtle pulsing grey blocks shaped like cards)
- [ ] On API error: render an error banner above the stats with "Couldn't load dashboard — retry" button
- [ ] Projects section renders a placeholder "Projects section coming soon"
- [ ] Activity section renders a placeholder "Activity feed coming soon"

## UAT Test Steps

1. Visit `/home-preview`.
   **Expected:** Lands on the new Home page. Page title is "Commander — Home". Header has logo + green dot + 2 icons only.

2. With 1 sprint running:
   **Expected:** Card 1 shows green border + animated flowing stripe + correct subtitle.

3. With 3 UAT-pending tickets:
   **Expected:** Card 2 shows amber number + correct subtitle.

4. With 0 of everything:
   **Expected:** All cards show 0 with "None" subtitles. No green border on card 1.

5. Hover card 1.
   **Expected:** Lifts 1px, shadow appears.

6. Click card 1 (Sprint running).
   **Expected:** Navigates to the running project's Sprint Mgmt page.

7. Click card 3 (Sprints planned).
   **Expected:** No navigation. Tooltip shows "Open a project to plan sprints".

8. Resize to mobile width.
   **Expected:** Cards stack to 1 column. Tap target still 44px+.

9. Throttle network in DevTools, refresh.
   **Expected:** Skeleton placeholders visible during load, then real cards.

10. Stop the backend and refresh.
    **Expected:** Error banner appears with retry button. Clicking retry refetches.

11. Tab through cards with keyboard.
    **Expected:** Each card receives focus. Pressing Enter triggers click action.

## Out of Scope

- Final route at `/` (handled in routing ticket)
- Sidebar (this is the Home page; sidebar is project-page chrome)
- Projects deck rendering (separate ticket)
- Activity feed rendering (separate ticket)
- Multi-running-sprint disambiguation modal
- Cross-project UAT-pending filtered view

## Notes for Implementer

- Use `home_page_final.html` mockup as the visual reference; copy the CSS variables and tokens
- The running-treatment CSS (green border + flowing stripe) should be defined in a shared class that the sprint card from the running-sprint ticket can also use
- Skeleton loaders: use `var(--surface-2)` background with subtle pulse animation
- When fetch fails, log to console with full error; show user-friendly banner only

Title: Home page Projects section — active cards + idle deck

Repo: zealchaiwut/commander

## What & Why

Build the Projects section of the Home page: active projects render as full-size cards in a row; idle projects render as a collapsing/expanding deck below. Click any project to navigate to its Sprint Mgmt page.

Mockup reference: `home_page_final.html` — section 2 (Projects).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Section renders below the stat cards from the previous ticket
- [ ] Section title row: "Projects · click to open" on the left, "<N> total" mono-font on the right
- [ ] **Classify each project at render time:**
  - **Active** = `status === "running"` OR `uat_count >= 1`
  - **Idle** = everything else
- [ ] **Active row** uses CSS grid: `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(320px, 1fr))`, gap 14px
- [ ] **Active project card** shows:
  - Top row: project icon (colored 26×26 badge with Tabler icon) + project name (16px, bold) + status pill on the right
  - Status pill: green "Running" with pulsing dot when running; amber "<N> UAT pending" when UAT-pending
  - Progress line: "Sprint <N> · <X> of <Y> done · <T> elapsed · est. <T> left" when running; "Last sprint: <label> · finished <T> ago" when UAT-pending
  - Progress bar: green fill with shimmer when running; amber fill when UAT-pending; thin (5px)
  - Meta row: UAT count + backlog count + (for running only) inline agent status "CODER working on #<num>"
- [ ] **Running active card** has green border + animated flowing top stripe (matches Sprint Running treatment)
- [ ] On hover: card lifts 1px, border darkens, shadow grows
- [ ] On click: navigates to `/project/<slug>/sprint-mgmt`
- [ ] **Idle deck section:**
  - Sub-header: stack icon + "Idle projects" + count badge + toggle hint on the right
  - Toggle hint: "click to expand ↓" when collapsed, "click to collapse ↑" when expanded
  - Default state: collapsed
  - Collapsed: top card full-size visible; next 3 cards peek out with 4/8/12px side offsets and opacity 0.85/0.65/0.45; cards 5+ stacked behind invisible
  - Expanded: cards arrange in `repeat(auto-fit, minmax(240px, 1fr))` grid, gap 10px
  - Cards fan in with staggered 40ms delay using `cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` easing
  - Click anywhere on the deck or header to toggle
- [ ] Each idle card shows:
  - Project icon + project name + "X ago" timestamp on the right of the top row
  - Meta row below: UAT count + backlog count (mono font, muted)
- [ ] Meta row on collapsed deck is hidden (only top row visible)
- [ ] Expanded state persists in `localStorage` key `commander.home.idleDeckExpanded`
- [ ] **Edge case:** if only 1 idle project, no deck — render as a single full-width card
- [ ] **Edge case:** if 0 active projects, omit the active row entirely; idle deck expands by default
- [ ] **Add tile** appears at the end of the idle grid (when expanded) OR below the deck (when collapsed and only 1 idle project): dashed border, "+ Add project" centered, opens existing add-project flow on click
- [ ] Deck header has `aria-expanded` reflecting state
- [ ] Touch devices: tap header to expand/collapse (no hover requirement)

## UAT Test Steps

1. With 1 active project (commander running) and 5 idle projects:
   **Expected:** Active row shows commander full-size in 1 column (or 2-3 on wide screens). Below: "Idle projects · 5" header with collapsed deck — top card visible, 3 cards peeking with decreasing opacity.

2. Click the deck header.
   **Expected:** Cards fan into a 2-3 column grid with staggered animation. Header text changes to "click to collapse ↑". "+ Add project" tile appears at end of grid.

3. Refresh the page.
   **Expected:** Deck remembers expanded state from localStorage.

4. Click commander's active card.
   **Expected:** Navigates to `/project/commander/sprint-mgmt`.

5. Resize to mobile width.
   **Expected:** Active cards stack to 1 column. Expanded deck cards stack to 1 column.

6. With 0 active projects and 3 idle projects:
   **Expected:** Active row is omitted. Idle deck is expanded by default.

7. With 1 idle project total:
   **Expected:** No deck — renders as single full-width card. "+ Add project" tile sits below it.

8. With 0 projects total:
   **Expected:** Section shows only "+ Add project" tile.

9. Click "+ Add project" tile.
   **Expected:** Opens the existing add-project flow.

10. Verify the running active card has green border + animated stripe.

11. Verify the running active card progress bar has shimmer animation.

12. Keyboard: Tab through cards.
    **Expected:** Each card focusable, Enter triggers navigation.

## Out of Scope

- Drag-to-reorder projects
- Pinning a project to always appear in the active row
- Custom project icon picker
- Multi-running-sprint disambiguation
- Card-level quick actions ("Run latest sprint" inline button)

## Notes for Implementer

- Idle deck CSS recipe: use `position: absolute` for cards in collapsed state, `position: relative` + grid in expanded state. CSS transition handles the morph between them. Use `:not(.is-expanded) .idle-card:nth-child(N)` selectors for the peek effect.
- The cubic-bezier `(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1)` is "ease-out-quart" — use consistently across animations.
- The active-card running treatment should reuse the CSS class from the stat card ticket
- For agent inline status on the active card, fetch from the same `/api/home` `projects[].sprint_running` payload — don't add a new endpoint
- Project icons: read color + Tabler icon name from `projects[].icon` field; if missing, fall back to `ti-folder` with neutral grey

Title: Home page Activity feed — last 5 events

Repo: zealchaiwut/commander

## What & Why

Build the Activity section of the Home page: a unified feed of the 5 most recent events across all projects. Each row links to the relevant project surface for that event.

Mockup reference: `home_page_final.html` — section 3 (Activity).

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Section renders below the Projects section
- [ ] Section title row: "Activity" on the left, "last 5 events" mono-font on the right
- [ ] Activity items render as vertical list with 8px gap
- [ ] Each item: rounded-corner card (border, 8px radius) with horizontal layout:
  - Left: 34×34 colored icon badge
  - Middle: title (14px, bold) + sub-line (12px, mono, muted)
  - Right: chevron-right icon for affordance
- [ ] Icon color treatment by event type:
  - `sprint_started` → green icon (loader/play)
  - `sprint_completed` → grey icon (check)
  - `ticket_moved_to_uat` → amber icon (eye-check)
  - `ticket_needs_rework` → red icon (x)
  - `sprint_failed` → red icon (alert)
- [ ] On hover: border darkens, light background tint
- [ ] On click: navigates to the `link` field from the API payload (typically `/project/<slug>/sprint-mgmt` or `/project/<slug>/tickets`)
- [ ] If `activity` array is empty: render empty state — small icon + "Nothing recent — try running a sprint from a project" (no giant graphic)
- [ ] Activity is fetched as part of `GET /api/home` (no separate request)
- [ ] Timestamps in sub-line render as humanized relative time on the client ("47m ago", "1d ago"); use a small lib like `dayjs` if not already loaded, otherwise hand-roll a tiny formatter (no new heavy dependency)
- [ ] Empty state center-aligned, muted color

## UAT Test Steps

1. With 5+ recent events across projects:
   **Expected:** Activity section shows exactly 5 items in reverse chronological order. Each has icon + title + sub + chevron.

2. Hover an activity item.
   **Expected:** Border darkens, slight background tint.

3. Click an activity item linked to `/project/commander/sprint-mgmt`.
   **Expected:** Navigates to that page.

4. With 0 recent activity (fresh install):
   **Expected:** Empty state message visible.

5. With 1 event of each type:
   **Expected:** Icons render in correct colors (green for running, amber for UAT, red for failures, grey for completed).

6. Inspect rendered timestamps.
   **Expected:** All render as relative time ("2h ago", not raw ISO).

7. Keyboard: Tab through activity items.
   **Expected:** Each focusable, Enter triggers navigation.

## Out of Scope

- Filtering activity by project / event type (logs sub-tab does that)
- Pagination beyond 5 events
- Real-time push of new events (page refresh is enough)
- Marking activity as "read" / dismissing items
- Custom event grouping ("3 sprints completed today")

## Notes for Implementer

- Don't pull in moment.js — too heavy. Either use dayjs (lightweight, ~2KB) or hand-write a 20-line relative-time formatter
- Activity icons: use Tabler icon classes; the badge color comes from CSS variables defined per-type
- If `link` field is missing on an event, render the item as non-clickable (no hover effect)
- Empty state should NOT auto-trigger a poll loop — the page refresh on next nav is enough

Title: Routing — Home replaces Overview, rename across codebase

Repo: zealchaiwut/commander

## What & Why

Cut over the new Home page to the root route `/`, rename "Overview" → "Home" throughout the codebase where it refers to the landing page, and add `/home` as an alias that redirects to `/`. This ticket is the final flip — ship after the other Home page tickets are deployed and working.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Route `/` renders the new Home page
- [ ] Route `/home` returns a 301 redirect to `/`
- [ ] Temporary preview route `/home-preview` is removed (or redirects to `/`)
- [ ] Old `/overview` route (if it exists) redirects to `/`
- [ ] Sidebar link on project pages reads "Home" with `ti-home` icon (not "Overview")
- [ ] Clicking the Commander brand mark in the header navigates to `/`
- [ ] HTML page title is "Commander — Home" on the root route
- [ ] All references to "Overview" in user-facing strings (page titles, button labels, link text, ARIA labels) that refer to the landing page are renamed to "Home"
- [ ] Do NOT rename usages of "overview" that refer to other concepts (e.g. "sprint overview" comments, "overview of code changes" etc.)
- [ ] Update README screenshots if any show "Overview" navigation
- [ ] Update CLAUDE.md if it references "Overview" page
- [ ] Tests that referenced `/overview` or "Overview" page are updated to use `/` or "Home"
- [ ] Delete the old Overview page React/HTML component file entirely

## UAT Test Steps

1. Visit `/`.
   **Expected:** New Home page renders.

2. Visit `/home`.
   **Expected:** 301 redirect to `/`.

3. Visit `/overview` (if it existed).
   **Expected:** Redirects to `/`.

4. Open a project page. Look at the sidebar.
   **Expected:** First link reads "Home" with house icon, not "Overview".

5. Click the Commander brand mark from any page.
   **Expected:** Returns to `/`.

6. Inspect page title in browser tab on root route.
   **Expected:** "Commander — Home".

7. Search codebase for "Overview" — manually review each match.
   **Expected:** Only matches related to non-landing-page concepts remain.

8. Run existing test suite.
   **Expected:** No failures from renamed routes / labels.

## Out of Scope

- Major redesign of the brand mark / logo
- Settings panel content (separate ticket)
- Removing the old top-level tabs (Overview / Agents / Activity log / Sprint) — that's a separate cutover ticket
- Adding new top-level tabs

## Notes for Implementer

- Ship LAST among Home tickets. Shipping this before backend + frontend tickets are deployed leaves the root route broken.
- Do a careful grep before renaming — "Overview" appears in non-landing-page contexts (e.g. sprint overview, code overview docs)
- The 301 redirect (not 302) for `/home` → `/` so browser caches the redirect
- After this ships, the dashboard's public URL surface is: `/`, `/project/<slug>/sprint-mgmt`, `/project/<slug>/tickets`, `/project/<slug>/logs`
- Update the README "Quick start" section to reflect the new Home landing page

Labels: enhancement, dashboard, navigation, cleanup, sprint-12
